topic: Happy Engineers Day: Honoring Sir M. Visvesvaraya and Everyday Problem-Solvers
commentary:
Happy Engineers' Day to everyone who looks at a broken, messy problem and says: 'Let's figure out how to make this work.'

Whether you build:
- Concrete bridges or cloud infrastructure
- Electrical grids or machine learning models
- Microchips, manufacturing lines, or mobile apps

The core job of an engineer is always the same:
Turning chaos into things that actually work under real-world pressure.

Today honors the birth anniversary of Bharat Ratna Sir M. Visvesvaraya. He didn't just build iconic dams and automated floodgates. He set the standard for what engineering means: solving hard, unglamorous problems that protect society quietly in the background.

Most people only notice engineering when something fails.
When a bridge cracks, when the power cuts out, or when a server goes down.

But when everything runs smoothly, safely, and on time?
That is thousands of engineers doing their job quietly while the rest of the world moves forward.

To every engineer, builder, and problem-solver:
Thank you for building the world we rely on every single day.

Happy Engineers' Day!

Which branch of engineering did you start your journey in?
